rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the opponents are portrayed as unusually aggressive, the verse foregrounds what they extend toward believers before naming the instrument.
rows.anchor: لما نسبهم للتعدي الزائد قدم ذكر المبسوط إليهم على الآلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sirius is singled out although God is Lord of everything because an Arab called Ibn Abi Kabsha worshiped Sirius and invited people to do likewise.
rows.anchor: خص الشعري بالذكر دون غيرها من النجوم وهو رب كل شيء لأن العرب ظهر فيهم رجل يعرف بابن أبي كبشة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses understand rather than simply know because fiqh conveys an increment beyond bare knowledge.
rows.anchor: ولم يقل لا تعلمون لما في الفقه من الزيادة على العلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham shows filial courtesy: he expresses fear that punishment might touch his father instead of declaring it will befall him, and uses the Merciful to appeal to him.
rows.anchor: حيث لم يصرح فيه بأن العذاب لاحق له ولكنه قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording names the Merciful rather than the Avenger or Omnipotent to soften Abraham’s appeal; an unattributed poem contrasts deprivation from different hands.
rows.anchor: ولهذا ذكر الرحمن ولم يذكر المنتقم ولا الجبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage asks why the consequence is expressed with mockery rather than repeating the earlier word istihzaʾ; it leaves the question open here.
rows.anchor: قد يقال ما الحكمة في التعمير بالسخرية دون الاستهزاء وهلا قيل فحاق بالذين استهزءوا بهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In affirmative clauses, putting an adverbial or prepositional phrase first generally marks exclusivity, assigning return, judgment, dominion, praise, and gathering to God alone.
rows.anchor: وأما تقديم الظرف ففيه تفصيل فإن كان في الإثبات دل على الاختصاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The witness phrase is delayed for the community because the point is their testimony over other peoples, but advanced for the Messenger to emphasize his testimony over them.
rows.anchor: أخرت صلة الشهادة في الأول وقدمت في الثاني لأن الغرض في الأول إثبات شهادتهم على الأمم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To the people means all people, Arabs and non-Arabs, because the definite article is universal.
rows.anchor: أي لجميع الناس من العجم والعرب على أن التعريف للاستغراق

words: لا فيها غول ولا هم عنها ينزفون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In a negative clause, fronting the phrase distinguishes the negated object from others: Paradise wine lacks the harm found in other wine.
rows.anchor: وإن كان في النفي فإن تقديمه يفيد تفضيل المنفى عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the phrase is delayed, the construction simply denies doubt in the matter; the contrast is illustrated by no fault in the house versus no fault in the house at all.
rows.anchor: وأما تأخيره فإنها تفيد النفي فقط

words: كلا هدينا ونوحا هدينا من قبل
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exclusivity effect of fronting is usual rather than necessary; the cited examples show that fronting does not invariably produce it.
rows.anchor: والذي عليه محققو البيانيين أن ذلك غالب لا لازم

rows.speaker: صاحب الفلك الدائر وابن الحاجب وأبو حيان
rows.claim: The author of al-Falak al-Dāʾir, Ibn al-Ḥājib, and Abū Ḥayyān reject the exclusivity rule, citing the first counterexample; al-Zarkashī says that qualifying it as usual resolves the dispute.
rows.anchor: وقد رد صاحب الفلك 7 الدائر القاعدة بالآية الأولى وكذلك ابن الحاجب والشيخ أبو حيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fronting counts as genuine only if the element is not inherently initial, such as an interrogative noun or a subject under the analysis that it is governed by its predicate.
rows.anchor: ألا يكون المعمول مقدما بالوضع فإن ذلك لا يسمى تقديما حقيقة كأسم الاستفهام وكالمبتدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second restriction is that fronting must not be required by the construction itself, as in the accusative reading of as for Thamud, We guided them.
rows.anchor: والثاني ألا يكون التقديم لمصلحة التركيب

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh says the alif and hāʾ attached to ayyā are emphatic, as though yā were repeated, and the noun becomes an attention signal.
rows.anchor: قال سيبويه واما الالف والهاء اللتان لحقتا اياه توكيدا فكانك كررت يا مرتين

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī calls the attention particle an insertion between adjective and described noun: it reinforces the vocative and replaces the genitive relation due after ayy.
rows.anchor: فقال وكلمة التنبيه المقحمه بين الصفة وموصوفها لفائدة تبيين معاضدة حرف النداء

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says using yā for a nearby addressee signals emphasis and special importance in the following address.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري انه للتأكيد المؤذن بان الخطاب الذي يتلوه معتنى به جدا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī argues that wāw enters a descriptive clause to emphasize the attribute’s establishment, as it does in circumstantial clauses.
rows.anchor: زعم الزمخشري انها تدخل على الجملة الواقعه صفة التأكيد ثبوت الصفة بالموصوف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Zarkashī rejects that analysis: the clause is circumstantial, since an exceptive construction with an omitted exception does not occur in adjectival clauses and village is general after illā.
rows.anchor: والصحيح ان الجملة الموضوف بها لاتقترن بالواو لان الاستثناء المفرغ لايقع في الصفات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional particle immā is formed from conditional in plus mā for emphasis; the source reports disagreement over how the emphatic nūn relates to that addition.
rows.anchor: اصلها ان الشرطية زيدت ما تأكيدا وكلام الزجاج يقتضي ان سبب اللحاق نون التوكيد

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī reverses al-Zajjāj’s account: mā is added because a conditional verb resembles a verb confirmed by oath, and mā adds emphasis.
rows.anchor: وقال الفارسي الامر بالعكس لمشابهة فعل الشرط بدخول ما للتأكيد بالفعل المقسم عليه

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ says all Qurʾanic conditional verbs after immā take nūn by analogy, since adding mā signals especially strong emphasis.
rows.anchor: قال أبو البقاء وهو القياس لان زيادة ما مؤذنة بارادة شدة التوكيد

rows.speaker: المبرد والزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Mubarrad and al-Zajjāj require the emphatic nūn on the conditional verb after immā, allowing omission only under poetic necessity.
rows.anchor: فقال المبرد والزجاج يلزم ولاتحذف الا ضرورة

rows.speaker: سيبويه وغيره
rows.claim: Sibawayh and other grammarians say the nūn is optional after immā, though retaining it is better; mā may also be omitted while nūn remains.
rows.anchor: وقال سيبويه وغيره لاتلزم فيجوز اثباتها وحذفها ولاثبات احسن ويجوز حذف ما واثبات النون

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh says mā and the emphatic nūn do not occur together in this construction; a poem is cited as usage without nūn after immā.
rows.anchor: قال سيبويه ان تثبت لم تقحم النون كما انك اذا أثبت لم تجيء بما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Numerals are ordered naturally from each rank to the next higher one: two, three, four, and likewise three/four or five/six in the cited examples.
rows.anchor: وكذلك جميع الأعداد كل مرتبة هي متقدمة على ما فوقها بالذات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exhortation puts people together before singly because collective counsel for God while leaving bias is the more important state; individuals then reflect as well.
rows.anchor: ولا شك أن الأهم حالة الاجتماع فبدأ بها

rows.speaker: محمد بن عيسى الأصبهاني
rows.claim: Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā al-Iṣfahānī reports that Basran codices write every Qurʾanic occurrence of luʾluʾ without alif except two places, in al-Ḥajj and al-Insān.
rows.anchor: وعن محمد بن عيسى الأصبهانى كل ما فى القرآن من لؤلؤ فبغير الألف فى مصاحف البصريين

rows.speaker: عاصم الجحدرى
rows.claim: ʿĀṣim al-Jaḥdarī says the ʿUthmānic codex writes all occurrences of luʾluʾ with alif except the one in Sūrat al-Malāʾika.
rows.anchor: وقال عاصم الجحدرى كلها فى مصحف عثمان بالألف إلا التى فى الملائكة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extra alif signals that Hell’s coming is an extraordinary, manifest appearance unlike familiar coming; the author links it with its exposure and being seen from afar.
rows.anchor: زيدت الألف دليلا على أن هذا المجىء هو بصفة من الظهور ينفصل بها عن معهود المجىء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alif is absent when the prophets and witnesses are brought in the familiar sense; it is also written when the phrase is interpreted as their manifestation at the gathering in honor of God.
rows.anchor: حيث لم تكتب الألف لأنه على المعروف فى الدنيا وفى تأوله بمعنى البروز فى المحشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extra alif in thing marks a future thing known through imagining an existing counterpart: it exists mentally but not yet in external reality.
rows.anchor: الشىء هنا معدوم وإنما علمناه من تصور مثله الذى قد وقع فى الوجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the thing in God’s Be command, its manner is unknown and affirmed by submission; God knows things by His knowledge, whereas humans know them through existence, without anthropomorphism or denial.
rows.anchor: بل نؤمن به تسليما لله سبحانه فيه فإنه سبحانه يعلم الأشياء بعلمه لا بها ونحن نعلمها بوجودها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added alif between lām and hamza in to Pharaoh and his chiefs marks a distinct, manifest particular.
rows.anchor: زيدت الألف بين اللام والهمزة تنبيها على تفصيل مهم ظاهر الوجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The extra alif in miʾa reflects that the word comprises a differentiated multitude in two orders, units and tens.
rows.anchor: ومثله زيادتها فى مائة لأنه اسم يشتمل على كثرة مفصلة بمرتبتين آحاد وعشرات

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr’s al-Muqniʿ says the connecting alif, silent in connected speech, is omitted in son of Mary when it is an epithet but retained in predicate constructions; it is omitted in only five places.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عمرو فى المقنع لا خلاف فى رسم ألف الوصل الناقصة من اللفظ فى الدرج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although God’s will is certain in the promised entry to the Sacred Mosque, the wording teaches people to say if God wills in every matter, following the command about tomorrow; it is an established practice.
rows.anchor: مع ان مشيئة الله محققه فجاء على تعليم الناس كيف يقولون وهم يقولون في كل شيء على جهة الاتباع

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet said, God willing, I will join you; the phrase may express uncertainty about when the joining will occur.
rows.anchor: ومثله قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم وانا ان شاء الله بكم لاحقون ويحتمل ان تكون للابهام في وقت اللحوق

rows.speaker: صاحب البسيط وابن الحاجب
rows.claim: The author of al-Basīṭ and Ibn al-Ḥājib distinguish temporal connectors: when is unsuitable for a known inevitable event in one construction, but works for an event conditioned on another.
rows.anchor: وابن الحاجب متى بان قال لاتقول متى طلعت الشمس

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says matā indicates an important but unspecified time, while idhā indicates a definite time; matā governs the jussive because of its temporal indeterminacy.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري في الفصل بين متى واذ ان متى للوقت المهم وإذا للمعين

words: قل إن كان للرحمن ولد فأنا أول العابدين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A conditional may be true even when its antecedent and consequent are impossible, because the antecedent implies the consequent; denying the consequent therefore denies the antecedent.
rows.anchor: قد يعلق الشرط بفعل محال يستلزمه محال آخر

words: لو كان فيهما آلهة إلا الله لفسدتا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Such hypothetical conditionals establish implication and infer that the antecedent is false from the consequent’s falsity; conditionals may concern established, impossible, or possible matters.
rows.anchor: وفائدة الربط بالشرط في مثل هذا امران احدهما بيان استلزام احدى القضيتين للأخرى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When a question particle precedes a conditional, its second clause is the matter asked about, not the conditional’s answer; the hamza is understood before that clause and the answer is omitted.
rows.anchor: والفعل الثاني الذي هو جزاء الشرط ليس جزاء للشرط وانما هو المستفهم عنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The implied question is whether they would turn back on their heels if Muḥammad died, and the purpose is to condemn such a reversal.
rows.anchor: والتقدير عنده أأنقلبتم على اعقابكم ان مات محمد لان الغرض انكار انقلابهم على اعقابهم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One account makes Quraysh the base of the seven dialects, alongside tribes near Mecca and later Tamim, Qays, and affiliated Arabian tribes; the Prophet’s fosterage among Saʿd b. Bakr is part of the explanation.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم أصل ذلك وقاعدته قريش ثم بنو سعد بن بكر لأن النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم استرضع فيهم

rows.speaker: قاسم بن ثابت
rows.claim: Qāsim b. Thābit says seven Mudar tribal dialects cover the Qurʾan’s linguistic forms; their eloquence and central Arabian location suited revelation and made its inimitability clear.
rows.anchor: قال قاسم بن ثابت إن قلنا من الأحرف لقريش ومنها لكنانة ولأسد وهذيل وتميم وضبة وألفافها وقيس

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Another view places all seven dialects within Mudar, citing ʿUthmān’s report that the Qurʾan was revealed in Mudar’s language and naming Quraysh, Kināna, Asad, Hudhayl, Dabba, and Ṭābikha.
rows.anchor: وقيل هذه اللغات السبع كلها فى مضر واحتجوا بقول عثمان نزل القرآن بلسان مضر

rows.speaker: أبو عمر بن عبد البر
rows.claim: Abū ʿUmar b. ʿAbd al-Barr reports critics who reject that all Mudar dialects occur in the Qurʾan because it avoids non-recited features such as Qays kashkasha, Tamim ʿanʿana, and changing sīn to tāʾ.
rows.anchor: قال أبو عمر بن عبد البر وأنكر آخرون كون كل لغات مضر فى القرآن لأن فيها شواذ لا يقرأ بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited Qays kashkasha turns the feminine second-person kāf into shīn, so under you is pronounced rabbish taḥtish in the verse about Mary.
rows.anchor: كشكشة قيس يجعلون كاف المؤنث شينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited Tamim ʿanʿana replaces hamza with ʿayn, pronouncing the hamza of an as ʿayn; the source also notes a dialect changing sīn in al-nās to tāʾ.
rows.anchor: وبعضهم يبدل السين تاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report that the Qurʾan was revealed in Quraysh’s language is stronger than the Mudar attribution because it comes through trustworthy Medinan transmitters.
rows.anchor: وهذا أثبت عنه لأنه من رواية ثقات أهل المدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that Gabriel would have to pronounce each word seven times applies only if seven letters converge in one word; al-Zarkashī says Gabriel brought one letter at each recitation until seven had passed.
rows.anchor: إنما يلزم هذا إن قلنا إن السبعة الأحرف تجتمع فى حرف واحد ونحن قلنا كان جبريل يأتى فى كل عرضة بحرف إلى أن تمر سبعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional particle is written separate in one verse because its fāʾ-linked result, the Messenger’s worldly delivery, is manifest; in the parallel wording the result is return to God and hidden.
rows.anchor: ظهر فيها حرف الشرط فى الخط لوجهين أحدهما أن الجواب المرتب عليه بالفاء ظاهر فى موطن الدنيا وهو البلاغ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first conditional’s answer divides into worldly proclamation and an appended account of judgment; the written separation marks this real distinction between visible and hidden outcomes.
rows.anchor: القصة الأولى منفصلة من الشرط وجوابه وانقسم الجواب إلى جزأين أحدهما الترتيب بالفاء وهو البلاغ والثانى المعطوف عليه وهو الحساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conditional is graphically explicit in al-Qaṣaṣ because its result concerns visible following of desires; in Hūd it is hidden because the result concerns the unseen descent of the Qurʾan with knowledge and tawḥīd.
rows.anchor: أظهر حرف الشرط فى الأول لأن جوابه المترتب عليه بالفاء هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All instances of an lan are written apart except in al-Kahf and al-Qiyāma, where the nūn is omitted graphically to signal the falsity of the claim and the absorption of its false emphasis into negation.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك أن لن كله مفصول إلا حرفان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the unbelievers’ claim that they will not be raised, the nūn remains visible because they themselves imagine and assert it; their denial is false about the afterlife but true of worldly life.
rows.anchor: فهؤلاء لم ينسبوا ذلك لفاعل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and others explain secret as what one conceals within oneself and more hidden as what has not yet occurred to one’s mind; both are equally known to God.
rows.anchor: فعن ابن عباس وغيره السر ما أسررت في نفسك وأخفى منه ما لم تحدث به نفسك مما يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording with more hidden is more emphatic; one analysis treats it as a comparative requiring an understood comparison, while another says it observes the verse endings.
rows.anchor: ولا شك أن الآتي أبلغ وفيه وجهان أحدهما أنه أفعل تفضيل يستدعي مفضلا عليه علم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Order may reflect the nobility of perception: hearing is placed before sight because it is nobler according to the stronger view among a group of scholars.
rows.anchor: ومنها شرف الإدراك كتقديم السمع على البصر والسميع على البصير لأن السمع أشرف على أرجح القولين عند جماعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heart precedes hearing and sight because the senses serve it and deliver information to it, and it is the intended recipient.
rows.anchor: لأن الحواس خدمة القلب وموصلة إليه وهو المقصود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heart is delayed here because the context condemns people who refuse to listen, including those who put cotton in their ears; the sūra opens by describing such hearers.
rows.anchor: فأخر القلب فيها لأن العناية هناك بذم المتصامين عن السماع ومنهم الذين كانوا يجعلون القطن في آذانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another basis for order is the superiority of reward, illustrated by mentioning the good deed and its reward before the evil deed.
rows.anchor: ومنها شرف العجازاة كقوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pardon precedes forgiveness because it is more general: it covers sins not exacted from people, while forgiveness concerns sins for which they were held to account in this world and then repented.
rows.anchor: فتقدم العفو على الغفور لأنه أعم وأخرت المغفرة لأنها أخص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Permissible things precede prohibited things when order honors permission; reversing the order intensifies rebuke or follows context, which first mentions lawful provision and then prohibited carrion.
rows.anchor: فللزيادة في التشنيع عليهم أو لأجل السياق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens precede earth among God’s unseen knowledge because their known contents are more numerous, making the order a stronger indication of omniscience.
rows.anchor: فقدم ذكر السموات لأن معلوماتها أكثر فكان تقديمها أدل على صفة العالمية

words: ماذا خلقوا من الأرض أم لهم شرك في السماوات
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earth comes first in the challenge to the idols because creating or sharing in it is far easier than in the heavens; failure at the easier task magnifies their incapacity.
rows.anchor: فبدأ بذكر الأرض لأنه في سياق تعجيز الشركاء عن الخلق والمشاركة وأمر الأرض في ذلك أيسر من السماء بكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens come first to emphasize divine power because they are greater than earth; ability to hold the greater entails ability to hold the lesser, but earth is also named for directness and clarity.
rows.anchor: فقدم السموات تنبيها على عظم قدرته سبحانه لأنه خلقها أكبر من خلق الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A word may be introduced early and repeated in closing position so the passage begins and ends with it, highlighting its importance.
rows.anchor: ومن أنواعه أن يقدم اللفظ في الآية ويتأخر فيها لقصد أن يقع البداءة والختم به للاعتناء بشأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trade-and-amusement wording begins with trade but concludes with trade after reversing their order, using the same beginning-and-ending pattern for emphasis.
rows.anchor: إذا رأوا تجارة أو لهوا انفضوا إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the angels’ report, hidden things are placed last to close on them, although knowledge of the hidden is more praiseworthy; other verses name secret before public matters.
rows.anchor: فإنه لولا ما أسلفناه لقيل ما تكتمون وتبدون لأن الوصف بعلمه أمدح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although secret and more hidden reverses the usual order that would put hidden knowledge last, the verse does so to preserve the rhyme of its endings.
rows.anchor: قلت لأجل تناسب رءوس الآى

words: ما يفتح الله للناس من رحمة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the preceding examples, mā is accusative because the verb acts directly upon it.
rows.anchor: في هذه المواضع في موضع نصب بوقوع الفعل عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Interrogative mā means what, takes the sentence’s initial position, and asks about objects or kinds and qualities of non-rational things, or qualities and kinds of rational beings.
rows.anchor: الثالث الاستفهامية بمعنى أي شىء ولها صدر الكلام كالشرط ويسأل بها اعيان ما لا يعقل

words: ما يدعون من دونه من شيء
rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl reads mā in the question about what people invoke besides God as interrogative: what thing do you invoke?
rows.anchor: قال الخليل في قوله تعالى ﴿ إن الله يعلم ما يدعون من دونه من شيء ﴾ 10 ما استفهام أي أي شىء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Interrogative mā can ask about qualities of rational beings; the relative pronoun mā has a comparable use in marry what is good for you of women.
rows.anchor: ومثال مجيئها لصفات من يعلم

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Rāghib reports that some grammarians permit interrogative mā for rational beings; al-Zarkashī argues Pharaoh asks about God’s attribute, since Moses answers with attributes, or else corrects an impossible question about divine essence.
rows.anchor: وجوز بعض النحويين أن يسأل بها عن أعيان من يعقل أيضا حكاه الراغب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The case of interrogative mā depends on what is asked: it is nominative as subject when it itself is asked about, but predicate when the following noun is the question’s subject.
rows.anchor: ثم فيه مسألتان إحداهما في إعرابها وهو بحسب الاسم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alif of interrogative mā is often dropped in genitive position so form matches meaning; it remains in nominative and accusative to avoid a one-letter word, while a preposition or annexed word supports it.
rows.anchor: ويكثر في حالة الخفض قصدوا مشاكلة اللفظ للمعنى فحذفوا الألف كما أسقطوا الصلة ولم يحذفوا في حال النصب والرفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They seek it crooked means they seek crookedness for it, with the preposition omitted.
rows.anchor: ويبغونها عوجا ﴾ 9 أي يبغون لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: We determined the moon means We determined for it, with the preposition understood.
rows.anchor: والقمر قدرناه ﴾ 1 أي قدرنا له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: We will return it to its former course means to its former course, with ʿalā understood before sīrata.
rows.anchor: سنُعيدها سيرتها ﴾ 2 أي على سيرتها

rows.speaker: أبو الحسن الشاذلي
rows.claim: Abū al-Ḥasan al-Shādhilī reconciles the commands by taking fear God as He deserves as referring to tawḥīd and as much as you can to deeds; the following call to die as Muslims supports this reading.
rows.anchor: أبي الحسن الشاذلي رحمه الله أنه جمع بينهما

rows.speaker: ابن المنير
rows.claim: Ibn al-Munīr says the second command abrogated the ruling of the first but not its merit or reward; the Prophet explained its maximal duty as obeying, remembering, and thanking God without lapse.
rows.anchor: قال ابن المنير الظاهر أن قوله

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report attributed here to the Prophet glosses complete God-fearing as obeying without disobedience, remembering without forgetfulness, and giving thanks without ingratitude; Ibn al-Munīr presents it as the basis for the later command.
rows.anchor: وقد فسر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: ابن المنير
rows.claim: On Ibn al-Munīr’s account, the initial duty required worship throughout life without interruption or sleep, like the fifty prayers before their reduction to five according to capacity, while the original rank remains.
rows.anchor: وكان التكليف أولا باستيعاب العمر بالعبادة بلا فترة ولا نعاس كما كانت الصلاة خمسين ثم صارت بحسب الاستطاعة خمسا

rows.speaker: كمال الدين الزملكاني
rows.claim: Kamāl al-Dīn al-Zamalkānī questions abrogation: doing what one can is itself complete God-fearing, which means adhering to God’s command and religion; many scholars share this view.
rows.anchor: وقال الشيخ كمال الدين الزملكاني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The report explaining complete God-fearing is not authentically traced to the Prophet; it is Ibn Masʿūd’s statement in al-Nasāʾī and does not include the companions’ objection or the claim that the second verse was revealed in response.
rows.anchor: لم يثبت مرفوعا بل هو من كلام ابن مسعود رواه النسائي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent conflict is resolved by distinguishing justice in the first verse, equitable fulfillment of wives’ rights, from the heart’s involuntary inclination in the second.
rows.anchor: والجواب أن المراد بالعدل في الأولى العدل بين الأزواج في توفية حقوقهن وهذا ممكن الوقوع وعدمه

words: ولن تستطيعوا أن تعدلوا بين النساء
rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet said after dividing time among his wives that this was his division in what he controlled and asked God not to hold him to account for what he did not control, namely the heart’s inclination.
rows.anchor: وقد كان صلى الله عليه وسلم يقسم بين نسائه ثم يقول

words: ولن تستطيعوا أن تعدلوا بين النساء
rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: ʿUmar prayed that he did not control his heart but hoped to be just in everything else.
rows.anchor: وكان عمر يقول ( الله قلبي فلا أملكه
